rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: both kings are tied down. Yours defends f4 and attacks f5; the black king does the same the other way round.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.e2: Whoever moves the king abandons their own pawn. Whoever has only king moves is in zugzwang: any move makes things worse.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.e3: What remains are the pawn moves on the a-file. Each one is a reserve tempo: it passes the turn without moving the king.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.e4: The two pawns will meet. When one stops in front of the other, both sides run out of reserve tempi.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.e5: Whoever makes the last pawn move leaves the opponent in zugzwang. That count decides the game.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.certo: Exactly! Your pawn advances just one square and keeps a reserve tempo for later.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.revela: The best is to advance the pawn one square, to a3, and keep the second tempo for later.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.err.a2a4.1: With that move, Black still has a reserve tempo and finds a resource.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.err.a2a4.2: The black pawn goes to a5 and blocks yours. Now it is your king that must move and abandon f4.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.err.g5h6.1: With that move, your king abandons the f4-pawn.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.err.g5h6.2: The black king captures the f4-pawn, and the f5-pawn has an open road.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.err.g5g6.1: With that move, your king abandons the f4-pawn.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.err.g5g6.2: The black king captures the f4-pawn, and the f5-pawn has an open road.

rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.err.g5f6.2: The black king captures the f4-pawn, and the f5-pawn has an open road.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.err.g5h5.1: With that move, your king abandons the f4-pawn.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.err.g5h5.2: The black king captures the f4-pawn, and the f5-pawn has an open road.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.err.g5h4.1: With that move, your king abandons the f4-pawn.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.err.g5h4.2: The black king captures the f4-pawn, and the f5-pawn has an open road.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.livre.fala: Keep playing with White and see how Black defends.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.fins.coroa: The pawn has promoted: the last pawn move was yours, and zugzwang decided it.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.fins.captura: The pawn has fallen. Before moving the king, count the reserve tempi on both sides.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.fins.afogado: The black king is stalemated: stalemate is a draw.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.fins.repetic: The position repeated: without the right reserve tempo, there was no progress.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.fins.limite: Without the right reserve tempo, White made no progress.

rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.l1: Now there are two empty squares between the pawns, a4 and a5, and it is Black to move.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.l2: Black uses the only reserve tempo they have: the pawn goes to a5.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.l3: And White closes the gap with the second tempo. The pawns are blocked.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.l4: Now Black is in zugzwang: only king moves are left, and all of them abandon f5.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.l6: Your king captures on f5. The f4-pawn is free, and the white king goes in front of it.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.l7: Now the count: between a2 and a6 there are three empty squares. Each one-square advance uses one of them.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.l8: Advancing one square, your pawn left two: one for each side. The last pawn move was yours.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.l9: Advancing two, it would leave only one, and the last pawn move would be Black’s.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex1.l10: The rule: after your move, leave an even number of empty squares between the pawns.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: the same structure, but the black pawn is already on a5. Count again.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex2.e2: Between the pawns there are now two empty squares, a3 and a4.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex2.certo: Exactly! The pawn advances two squares and blocks the black one. No empty square is left, and it is Black to move.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex2.revela: The best is to advance the pawn two squares, to a4: no empty square is left, and it is Black to move.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex2.err.a2a3.1: With that move, the win slips away: one empty square is left for Black.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex2.err.a2a3.2: The black pawn goes to a4 and closes the gap. Now it is your king that must abandon f4.

rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex2.livre.fala: Keep playing with White and see how Black defends.

rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex2.l1: The pawns are blocked, with no empty square between them, and it is Black to move.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex2.l2: Black is in zugzwang: the black king has to move and abandons f5.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex2.l4: Your king captures on f5 and clears the way for the f4-pawn.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex2.l5: Here the two-square advance was right. Zero is an even number too.
rot.secondReserve.ideia.ex2.l6: Keeping the reserve does not always mean moving one square: it means making sure the last pawn move is yours.
rot.secondReserve.demos.duasVezes.1: Attack: the pawns on the c- and g-files are blocked. The kings face each other, and it is White to move.
rot.secondReserve.demos.duasVezes.2: Black has the opposition. Only the c2-pawn can pass the turn, and it has two reserve tempi.
rot.secondReserve.demos.duasVezes.3: First, a single tempo: the pawn goes to c3.
rot.secondReserve.demos.duasVezes.4: Without the opposition, the black king has to give way. It goes to d7.
rot.secondReserve.demos.duasVezes.6: The black king returns to e7, facing your king, and regains the opposition.
rot.secondReserve.demos.duasVezes.7: White uses the second tempo, and the black king has to give way again.
rot.secondReserve.demos.duasVezes.8: The black king goes to d7.
rot.secondReserve.demos.duasVezes.9: Your king gets in via f6 and will capture the g6-pawn.
rot.secondReserve.demos.duasVezes.10: Now see what happens if the pawn spends both tempi at once.
rot.secondReserve.demos.duasVezes.11: The pawn goes straight to c4.
rot.secondReserve.demos.duasVezes.12: After the same manoeuvre, the black king regains the opposition on e7.
rot.secondReserve.demos.duasVezes.13: Now the c4-pawn has no move left. Your king has to give way, and Black holds the draw.
rot.secondReserve.demos.duasVezes.14: With two reserve tempi, spend them one at a time: you will need the second one later.
rot.secondReserve.demos.resposta.1: Defense: now let us think from Black’s side. The structure is the same, with pawns on a2 and a7.
rot.secondReserve.demos.resposta.2: There are four empty squares between them, and it is White to move. Black answers by the same count.
rot.secondReserve.demos.resposta.3: White advances one square: three empty squares are left.
rot.secondReserve.demos.resposta.4: Black also advances one square and leaves two: an even number.
rot.secondReserve.demos.resposta.5: White uses the second tempo and leaves one square.
rot.secondReserve.demos.resposta.6: And Black closes the gap. It is White to move, with no reserve tempo left.
rot.secondReserve.demos.resposta.7: White is in zugzwang: the white king has to abandon f4.
rot.secondReserve.demos.resposta.8: And what if White advances two squares right away?
rot.secondReserve.demos.resposta.9: Two empty squares are left, a5 and a6.
rot.secondReserve.demos.resposta.10: Black advances two squares and closes the gap: once again, it is White to move.
rot.secondReserve.demos.resposta.11: Now the mistake Black must avoid.
rot.secondReserve.demos.resposta.12: After White’s one-square advance, Black advances two: one empty square is left.
rot.secondReserve.demos.resposta.13: White closes the gap, and now it is Black who is in zugzwang.
